Welcome to St Edmund's Catholic Primary School
Our school is a welcoming, happy school where people are helpful, considerate and respectful of each other. Our school is a vibrant, positive place that provides a safe and welcoming environment in which to learn. As a Catholic School, we seek to live out the values of Jesus Christ. We promote these values by our words and deeds and recognising that every child is unique and is created in the image of God. Through our mission statement, “Through Christ, We Learn” we are dedicated to ensuring that our children uphold these values every day.
We are very fortunate to have such a dedicated team of teachers, support staff and other members of our school team, who strive to ensure that every child is successful, confident and responsibly, equipped with all the skills they need to continue on their future learning journey. Staff encourage the children to engage in our wide and varied curriculum and provide an atmosphere where children can fully develop their talents and learn new skills. We have carefully designed our curriculum to develop thinking skills, creativity and spirituality, encouraging confidence and opportunities for children to be excited about learning and challenged to achieve their very best.
We aim to cultivate first class partnerships with parents and carers, governors, our parish and the local community who play such an important part in the life of our thriving school.
I hope our new school website will give our parents, carers and prospective parents an insight into the life of St. Edmund’s Catholic Primary School. We warmly encourage families to arrange a tour of our wonderful school community so that you may see learning in action. Please do not hesitate to contact our School Office if there is anything else you would like to know about our school.
Thank you once again.
Dear Parents and Carers,
It is a joy to welcome you to St Edmund’s Catholic Primary School. Our mission is simple: “Through Christ we learn.” Every child here is seen as God’s masterpiece (Ephesians 2:10), created with unique gifts to grow in faith, wisdom, and love.
Guided by our SPIRIT values — Service, Perseverance, Integrity, Respect, Inclusivity, and Trust — we strive to provide an education where children flourish academically, spiritually, and personally. As Jesus reminds us, “You are the light of the world” (Matthew 5:14), and it is our privilege to help each child shine.
Thank you for entrusting your child to our care. We look forward to working in partnership with you.
With every blessing,

Religious Education In St Edmund's Catholic Primary School
Religious Education at St Edmund’s
Our Vision
At St Edmund’s Catholic Primary School, Religious Education (RE) is at the heart of everything we do. Rooted in our mission “Through Christ, we learn”, our RE curriculum nurtures children’s faith, deepens their knowledge, and helps them to grow as compassionate, thoughtful, and responsible individuals.
We follow the Religious Education Directory (RED, 2023), which sets out the national programme of study for Catholic schools in England and Wales. The RED provides a clear and progressive framework, ensuring that all pupils are taught with theological depth, creativity, and a spirit of encounter.
RE Curriculum Map
Our curriculum is built around the six thematic branches of RED:
Creation and Covenant – exploring God as Creator and His promises to His people.
Prophecy and Promise – reflecting on the Old Testament prophets and God’s promise of salvation.
Galilee to Jerusalem – following Jesus’ life, ministry, and teaching.
Desert to Garden – meditating on Christ’s Passion, Death, and Resurrection.
To the Ends of the Earth – encountering the birth of the Church and the mission of the apostles.
Dialogue and Encounter – learning about other world faiths and building respect for all people.
Each branch is revisited throughout a child’s journey at St Edmund’s, allowing knowledge, skills, and faith to develop in a spiral of progression.
[Download RE Curriculum Map below]
Skills and Knowledge Progression in Religious Education
At St Edmund’s, we follow the Religious Education Directory (RED 2023), which sets out a clear and ambitious progression of skills and knowledge from Nursery to Year 6.
Our progression is built around the six branches of study:
Creation and Covenant
Prophecy and Promise
Galilee to Jerusalem
To the Ends of the Earth
Dialogue and Encounter
Through these, pupils develop in three key areas of knowing:
Understand – building secure theological knowledge of Scripture, belief, sacraments, and the life of the Church.
Discern – interpreting, analysing, and making connections between faith, life, and the wider world.
Respond – reflecting personally, applying Gospel values, and living out Catholic Social Teaching in action.
Progression is carefully sequenced across year groups so that:
Early Years pupils retell and recognise key stories of Jesus and creation.
Key Stage 1 pupils begin to describe religious actions, symbols, and stories of faith.
Lower Key Stage 2 pupils explain how belief shapes life and make links across Scripture and tradition.
Upper Key Stage 2 pupils evaluate and apply Catholic teaching, express reasoned views, and lead worship and social action.
[Download our full RE Skills and Knowledge Progression Document]
Curriculum Intent & Enrichment
Our intent is to provide a curriculum that is:
Faith-centred: rooted in Scripture, Tradition, and the teachings of the Church.
Engaging: enriched with drama, art, music, debate, ICT, and creative writing.
Inclusive: respectful of diversity, encouraging dialogue with other world faiths.
Challenging: enabling all pupils to achieve theological literacy, critical thinking, and a personal response of faith.
Enrichment opportunities include:
School Masses and liturgies in partnership with our parish.
Class saint projects and feast day celebrations.
Visits to churches, synagogues, mosques, and other places of worship.
RE Creative Arts Week and inter-school competitions.
Cross-curricular links with history, art, drama, and social action.
RE in Action
Displays: Every classroom and corridor features RE displays that reflect the liturgical year and pupil learning.
Work Samples: Pupils’ RE work includes essays, theological reflections, art, drama, and digital projects. QR codes in displays showcase drama and musical performances.
Celebration of the Word: Weekly assemblies link the Gospel, our mission, and Catholic Social Teaching.
RE & Catholic Life: Progress from 2024 to 2026
St Edmund’s Catholic Primary School
At St Edmund’s, pupil voice is central to how we grow as a Catholic community. In 2024, we gathered a full baseline of pupils’ experiences of RE, Collective Worship, Catholic Social Teaching (CST), and prayer life. Their feedback shaped our priorities and guided our mission over the next two years.
In 2026, we repeated the pupil voice process with a richer set of questions, deeper reflection, and more opportunities for pupils to express what matters to them. The results show clear progress, stronger confidence, and a deepening of Catholic identity across the school.
What We Learned in 2024
The 2024 baseline showed:
Pupils enjoyed RE and felt they learned well
Collective Worship and prayer were fully embedded
Class saints were well understood
CST understanding was emerging
Creative learning and pupil leadership were areas for development
This gave us a strong foundation — and a clear direction.
What We Did in Response (2024–2026)
Following the 2024 findings, we:
Strengthened RE teaching through more creative approaches
Improved assessment and feedback
Made CST more visible across the school
Increased pupil leadership in Collective Worship
Developed dedicated prayer spaces
Deepened teaching about class saints
Expanded opportunities for pupils to share their voice
These actions shaped the experience pupils reported in 2026.
Progress by 2026
The 2026 pupil voice shows clear growth across RE and Catholic Life:
High enjoyment of RE and strong engagement in lessons
Greater confidence in explaining Bible stories and using RE vocabulary
Clear understanding of what teachers expect in RE
CST more deeply embedded, with pupils confidently naming and explaining key themes
Collective Worship valued, with strong participation and increasing pupil leadership
Prayer fully embedded as part of daily school life
Charity and social action more visible, with pupils able to explain why it matters
Creative learning recognised as helping pupils understand scripture and RE concepts
Impact on Our Catholic Community
Between 2024 and 2026, pupil voice shows:
Stronger RE outcomes
Greater confidence in scripture and vocabulary
CST embedded in daily life
Worship that is more reflective, reverent, and pupil-led
Prayer life that is consistent and meaningful
Pupils who can articulate what helps them learn and grow in faith
A school culture where creativity, reverence, and Catholic identity flourish
St Edmund’s has grown in faith, understanding, and unity.
Next Steps for 2026–2027
Guided by pupil voice, our next steps are to:
Increase creative RE (art, drama, music, role play)
Deepen scripture understanding through storytelling and acting
Strengthen CST visibility and real-life application
Expand pupil-led worship opportunities
Enhance prayerful atmosphere with music and reflective spaces
Continue clarifying expectations and strengthening vocabulary
Increase charity and social action projects
Use devices to support engagement and understanding
These steps ensure that RE and Catholic Life continue to grow in depth, joy, and meaning.
At St Edmund’s, pupil voice is not a one‑off exercise — it is a living part of our mission. Our children help shape the Catholic life of the school, and their insights guide us as we continue to grow in faith, love, and learning.

Pupil Leadership for Justice, Inclusion and Faith
Pupil Leadership for Justice, Inclusion & Faith
At St Edmund’s Catholic Primary School, we believe that pupil leadership is a living expression of our Catholic mission.
Through dedicated pupil groups, our children grow as leaders of faith, justice, inclusion, and stewardship, bringing our Gospel values to life in every aspect of school life.
Each group is trained and commissioned to serve others, to lead prayer and action, and to represent the voice of pupils in shaping our Catholic community. Together they form our Pupil Leadership Team for Justice, Inclusion & Faith — the heart of our Catholic Life and Mission.
Peace & Justice Society
“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.” – Matthew 5:9
Our Peace & Justice Society leads the school in prayer, service, and action. They teach others about Catholic Social Teaching, promote kindness and fairness, and remind us that every child can be an agent of change.
Lead weekly classroom visits and reflections on peace, justice, and Gospel values.
Organise fundraising and service projects through Harvest, Lent, and Advent.
Represent St Edmund’s at diocesan Peace & Justice events.
Support Caritas and parish outreach.
[View their PowerPoint Presentation →]
Equality & Inclusion Ambassadors
“There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.” – Galatians 3:28
Our Equality & Inclusion Ambassadors ensure that every pupil feels valued, respected, and safe. They lead our RJED Strategy (Racial Justice, Equality & Diversity) through pupil-led initiatives and campaigns that celebrate the richness of our school community.
Plan assemblies for Anti-Bullying Week, Black History Month, and Interfaith Week.
Promote kindness, respect, and a sense of belonging.
Conduct pupil surveys on inclusion and share findings with leaders.
Celebrate cultural diversity through International Day and language projects.
[View their PowerPoint Presentation →]
Environmental Ambassadors (Laudato Si') – Guardians of Creation
“The Earth is our common home.” – Pope Francis, Laudato Si’*
Our Environmental Ambassadors lead the school in caring for creation and living out Laudato Si’ – Care for Our Common Home. They remind us that stewardship of the Earth is part of our faith and our duty to God.
Lead Laudato Si’ assemblies and Eco Action Days.
Maintain our Prayer Garden and outdoor learning spaces.
Promote recycling, energy saving, and zero-waste habits.
Organise community planting projects and eco pledges.
[View their PowerPoint Presentation →]
Caritas Ambassadors
“Through Christ, we learn.”
Our Caritas Ambassadors are Year 5 and 6 pupil leaders who bring faith into action. They help our school live out the seven themes of Catholic Social Teaching, leading acts of kindness, fundraising, and community outreach — locally, nationally, and globally.
Coordinate class Caritas actions across the year.
Lead Harvest, Lent, and CAFOD campaigns.
Build links with parish, CAFOD, and Caritas Westminster.
Inspire others through assemblies and displays of faith in action.
[View their PowerPoint Presentation →]
Why Pupil Leadership Matters
Through these groups, children develop confidence, empathy, and faith-driven leadership. They learn to speak up for what is right, serve others, and bring Gospel values into daily life — a visible sign of our Catholic identity in action.

Our mission: “Through Christ, We Learn”

healthy friendships and relationships
family life and caring for others
emotional wellbeing and mental health
personal boundaries and keeping safe
understanding their bodies and changes as they grow
online behaviour and digital safety

assemblies and themed weeks (Anti-Bullying, Online Safety, Mental Health)
RE and Catholic Social Teaching
Inclusion, safeguarding and wellbeing activities
classroom lessons linked to personal development
Children learn about:
kindness, respect and inclusion
responsibilities and community
decision-making and resilience
healthy lifestyles and mental wellbeing
safety in school, at home and online
living out British Values in a Catholic context
Together, RSE and PSHE help children understand themselves, value others and grow in confidence and character.

Mission Statement – “Through Christ We Learn”
At St Edmund’s, our mission statement is not something we only display on a wall — it is something we truly believe in and try to live every single day.
“Through Christ We Learn”
captures who we are as a community and what we hope for every child who walks through our doors.
From the moment you step into our school, you can sense the warmth, welcome and care that flow from this mission. You see it in the way pupils greet each other, in the peaceful prayer tables in each classroom, and in the gentle, encouraging relationships between staff and children.
Our mission echoes Jesus’ words:
“Let the little children come to me.” (Matthew 19:14)
Here, every child is welcomed, cherished and known by name.
It is also rooted in Christ’s invitation:
“Learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart.” (Matthew 11:29)
These words shape the way we teach, the way we support one another, and the way we help our children grow in confidence, empathy and resilience.
And most of all, our mission is lived.
It comes to life when a child stops to comfort someone who is upset. It shows itself when our Peace & Justice Leaders share the Sunday Gospel and offer a meaningful “mission” for the week ahead. It appears in the smiles of pupils helping younger children during worship. It shines when our community gathers at Mass to pray together:
“The Lord is my light and my salvation.” (Psalm 27:1)
Guided by the example of our school saint, St Edmund of Abingdon, we teach our pupils that learning is not only about subjects and skills. It is also about growing into the kind, thoughtful and courageous person God created them to be.
We remind them of Jesus’ promise:
“I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.” (John 10:10)
And you can see the mission being lived across our school every day:
In the quiet moments of prayer and reflection
In Celebration of the Word every Monday
In the Prayer Garden where children write prayers, give thanks, or reflect in silence
In the service projects led by our Caritas Ambassadors and Eco Team
In the thoughtful acts of kindness, fairness and forgiveness that happen naturally between children
In the SPIRIT values — Service, Perseverance, Integrity, Respect, Inclusivity, Trust — which guide our choices and relationships
Whether in a lesson, a playground conversation, a whole-school assembly or a simple act of kindness, our children learn that Christ is with them — supporting them, encouraging them, and helping them grow.
This is what our mission means to us:
We learn with Christ.
We learn through Christ. We learn to be more like Christ.
At St Edmund’s, “Through Christ We Learn” is not just our motto. It is our way of being a school. It is the story we tell. And it is the life we share.

Links with parents - Prayer at home
Assemblies & Parent Participation at St Edmund’s
At St Edmund’s, we deeply value the partnership between home and school, and we warmly welcome parents and carers to join us in celebrating our faith, values, and children’s achievements throughout the year.
Celebration of the Word
Every Monday | 9:00–9:15 a.m. (except the first Monday after half terms and holidays) Led by our Peace & Justice Group, this weekly gathering reflects on Sunday’s Gospel, introduces our Mission for the Week, and helps set a prayerful tone for our school community.
SPIRIT Assembly
Last Friday of each month In this whole-school assembly, we celebrate pupils who have lived out our SPIRIT values — Service, Perseverance, Integrity, Respect, Inclusivity and Trust — through:Star AwardsDoodle & Dojo AwardsAttendance Celebrations
Additional Events
We regularly host seasonal liturgies, feast-day celebrations, class assemblies and other special events. Parents will always receive information in advance, but as a general rhythm, you are invited to join us:
Every Monday morning (Celebration of the Word)
The last Friday of each month (SPIRIT Assembly)
Your presence strengthens our community, supports our children, and reflects the loving, inclusive ethos that defines St Edmund’s.
Thank you for your continued support and partnership.
Home Prayer Books at St Edmund’s
Growing Prayerful Hearts at Home
At St Edmund’s, prayer is a joyful part of our daily rhythm, and our Home Prayer Books help bring this experience into family life. Each class has a special prayer book linked to their class saint, and a different child takes it home every Friday. Families are invited to spend a quiet moment together—writing a simple prayer, drawing a picture, or reflecting on themes such as gratitude, kindness, creation or courage. These beautifully personal pages show children growing in faith, confidence and spiritual awareness, while helping them see prayer as a natural part of everyday life.
Strengthening the Home–School–Parish Journey
The Home Prayer Books complement our rich prayer and liturgical life at school: daily classroom prayer, weekly Celebration of the Word, pupil-led worship, seasonal liturgies, parish Masses, and reflective prayer spaces across every floor. Together, these practices nurture a strong partnership between home, school and parish, helping our pupils deepen their relationship with God and live our mission with joy: “…through Christ we learn.”
St Edmund’s RE & Catholic Life Newsletter
Celebrating Faith, Learning and Community
Our RE & Catholic Life Newsletter is a beautiful snapshot of the rich spiritual life at St Edmund’s. Each edition highlights the Gospel themes we are exploring, the prayer and worship taking place across the school, and the many ways our children put their faith into action through Catholic Social Teaching, leadership roles, and charitable work. Parents can also see photographs of class prayer tables, RE learning, liturgical celebrations, and pupil-led worship such as our weekly Celebration of the Word.
The newsletter is designed to help families stay connected with the rhythm of our Catholic life. It includes prayer ideas, Scripture reflections, key dates, parish links, and updates from groups such as our Peace & Justice Society, Caritas Ambassadors, School Council, and Parent Prayer Group. Through these regular updates, we continue strengthening the partnership between home, school, and parish so that our mission — “…through Christ we learn…” — is lived with joy both in school and at home.
Staying Connected Through ClassDojo
Sharing Our Faith, Learning and Community Moments
At St Edmund’s, we love keeping our families connected to the life of the school. Alongside our RE Newsletter, we regularly share updates on ClassDojo, where parents can see photos and posts celebrating the wonderful things happening each week. From classroom prayer, RE lessons and Gospel reflections to assemblies, feast-day celebrations, charity events, fundraising initiatives and parish links, ClassDojo allows families to witness our Catholic life unfolding in real time.
We also upload newsletters, reminders and key dates linked to the liturgical year, including Advent, Lent, Holy Week, saints’ feast days and whole-school worship. This helps parents feel informed, involved and able to share in their child’s learning and faith journey. Through ClassDojo, we continue strengthening our partnership with families—celebrating, communicating and growing together in our mission: “…through Christ we learn.”
